title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-iam-networking-migration
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private installer and Terraform modules have diverged across several repos and environments. This PR unifies the Terraform state layout for Private deployments, consolidates GPU node-pool, IAM role, and networking module layouts, and provides a documented, automated migration path for existing customer states. The goal is to make upgrades predictable for on-prem and VPC setups, reduce duplication, and enable per-tenant state scoping required by recent Dedicated/Private feature work.

What this changes (high level):
- Introduces a unified state path convention: private/<env>/<cluster>/<component> and migration helpers for legacy state paths.
- Refactors gpu_node_pools module to support per-cluster and per-tenant naming, idempotent upgrades, and optional node pool lifecycle flags.
- Adds explicit iam module roles/policies for private control-plane + workload, removing inlined role templates from caller modules.
- Network module updates: creates deterministic subnet naming, moves VPC-peering and route attachments into network module to avoid cross-module state drift.
- Adds comprehensive migration scripts (terraform state mv wrappers and a dry-run flag) and a small Go-based helper (build included) to validate state before changes.

Migration plan and operator notes:
1) Read the migration plan in docs/migrations/private-state-layout.md before applying.
2) Run ./scripts/terraform-migrate --dry-run to enumerate state moves. Review the proposed mappings.
3) For each environment run ./scripts/terraform-migrate apply --env <env> --bucket <state-bucket> --path <legacy-path>. The script will create a backup of the remote state and perform state moves with retries.
4) For clusters with GPU nodes: verify the new node pool resource addresses produced by the dry-run and ensure autoscaling tags are preserved.
5) Post-migration: apply a no-op terraform apply against the unified layout to confirm plan is empty.

Compatibility & rollback:
- Backups: script makes a timestamped copy of the remote state (S3/GCS) before mutating.
- Rollback: restore the backup and re-run terraform init/plan against the previous layout. The script prints exact restore commands.
- If a manual fix is required the migration output maps old->new addresses for targeted terraform state mv commands.

Testing & validation performed: 
- Unit tests for terraform modules via terraform-compliance targets.
- End-to-end dry-run against a staging S3 bucket with a copy of several customer states (sanitized) to validate address mappings.
- CI runs: lint, fmt, unit module tests, and the migration dry-run; all checks passed.
- Canary apply performed in a sandbox cluster (internal-only) and verified node reattach/rehydration for GPU pools.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: state move mistakes could orphan resources. Mitigation: automated backups, dry-run, conservative default flags and manual review step.
- Risk: IAM policy name changes might break tooling that depends on specific ARNs. Mitigation: maintained backward-compatible role outputs, and a deprecation window with mapping table in docs.

Files of interest and high-level diffs: see changed_files. Small snippets included where helpful (e.g., new state path conventions and migration helper CLI).

Release notes: "Unify Terraform private state layout and add automated migration for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking modules. Operators must run the provided migration tool per-environment; see docs/migrations/private-state-layout.md for details."

Related: this PR was coordinated with the private-installer and helm-chart changes in ENG-4921, and a follow-up will update the installer to reference the unified module outputs.

If you are reviewing: focus on the migration helper logic, state mapping table in docs, and the IAM policy renames (search for iam/policy/legacy -> iam/policy/v2).
